0. Data Management & Preprocessing¶

0.1 Import & Preprocess Data (Create Datasets D1/D2)¶

The following cell relies on function import_and_preprocess_data to load and prepare a dataset for modeling. It uses a given CSV file when provided; otherwise falls back to a previously saved, subgroup-annotated CSV file (enabling reproducible reruns that reuse existing dataset splits).

Behavior:

  • default mode: When dataset_path is provided and exists, the function
    1. reads the CSV,
    2. cleans/casts columns using imported lists: numerical_features and categorical_features,
    3. splits into preprocess/final sets with scikit-learn's train_test_split, and
    4. saves the organized data with a subgroup column (0 for identifying the preprocessing dataset, 1 for identifying the final evaluation dataset) to directory organized_subgroups_path.
  • Fallback mode: When dataset_path is None, it loads the file at organized_subgroups_path and reconstructs the two splits from the previously-created subgroup column.

Returns:

  • X_preprocess (pd.DataFrame)
  • X_final (pd.DataFrame)
  • y_preprocess (pd.Series)
  • y_final (pd.Series)

Here X_preprocess and y_preprocess correspond to the preprocessing dataset (D1, subgroup = 0), which is used for feature ranking/selection and machine learning hyperparameter tuning (via cross-validation). On the other hand, X_final and y_final correspond to the held-out dataset (D2, subgroup = 1), which is used exclusively to obtain unbiased ROC AUC performance estimates after features and hyperparameters have been selected/tuned on the preprocessing dataset D1.

Key parameters:

  • numerical_features, categorical_features: columns coerced to numeric and category.
  • target_variable: target column name (must exist after organization).
  • drop_features: columns removed before modeling (used by the default mode).
  • organized_subgroups_path: path to save/load the subgroup-annotated CSV.
  • split_test_size, split_random_state, stratify_on_target: control the split (stratify by target when True).

Notes:

  • If dataset_path is provided but missing, a FileNotFoundError is raised.
  • In fallback mode, the file must contain subgroup with values {0, 1}.
In [2]:
X_preprocess, X_final, y_preprocess, y_final = import_and_preprocess_data(
    numerical_features=numerical_features,
    categorical_features=categorical_features,
    target_variable="burst_aaa",
    # dataset_path="data/original_dataset.csv",
    drop_features=drop_features,
    organized_subgroups_path="data/original_dataset_with_subgroups_column.csv",
)

# Rename features, i.e., the columns in the dataset 
X_preprocess = X_preprocess.rename(columns=feature_name_mapping)
X_final = X_final.rename(columns=feature_name_mapping)

0.2 Feature Importance Ranking & Selection with ShapFire¶

In the following cells, we apply ShapFire to identify and select the most informative features. The method combines SHAP-based feature importance with repeated cross-validation to provide a stable, reproducible ranking. All computations are performed on the preprocessing dataset D1 to avoid information leakage into the held-out set D2.

Key parameters:

  • Estimator: LGBMClassifier with objective="binary" (other hyperparameters are tuned later).
  • Scoring: ROC AUC ("roc_auc").
  • Cross-validation: n_splits × n_repeats repeated k-fold CV applied on D1.
  • Iterations: Number of candidate feature subsets fitted in order to derive SHAP importance values.

Results:

  • A cross-validated, stable ranking of all features.
  • A selected subset of features (FS1), chosen by ShapFire for use in downstream model training and evaluation.
In [3]:
# Prepare input parameters for the ShapFire method
estimator_class = lgb.LGBMClassifier
estimator_params = {"objective": "binary"}
scoring = "roc_auc"
n_splits = 2
n_repeats =  2

sf = ShapFire(
  estimator_class=estimator_class,
  scoring=scoring,
  estimator_params=estimator_params,
  n_splits=n_splits,
  n_repeats=n_repeats,
  iterations=X_preprocess.columns.shape[0],
)
In [4]:
%%capture
# Perform feature importance ranking and selection
_ = sf.fit(X=X_preprocess, y=y_preprocess);

In the following, we visualize the distribution of normalized SHAP feature importance values across cross-validation runs for each feature. These plots highlight both the stability (consistency across folds) and the relative ranking of features.

The visual summary gives an intuitive overview of which features were most consistently influential and which subset was ultimately chosen as feature subset FS1.

_, _ = sf.plot_importance(plot_type="boxplot")

0.4 Model Comparison Plan¶

In the subsequent sections, we compare models trained and tuned with different feature sets:

  • FS1: ShapFire-selected features (listed above).
  • FS2: A single feature Maximal anterior-posterior diameter (cm).
  • FS3: All available features in the dataset.

The steps executed in the following for each feature set, can be summarized as follows:

  • Hyperparameter tuning happens on D1 (using repeated k-fold CV and ROC AUC as the performance measure).
  • The final performance is estimated on D2 (using repeated k-fold CV, with fixed features and hyperparameters).

The purpose here to avoid information leakage and make sure unbiased estimates are obtained.

1. Model M1: ShapFire-Selected Features (FS1)¶

1.1 Hyperparameter Tuning on D1¶

We tune LGBMClassifier hyperparameters on D1 using repeated k-fold CV with ROC AUC as the performance measure. The grid of values below define the used search ranges:

  • n_estimators: [100, 250, 500, 1000, 2000]
  • learning_rate: [0.070, 0.0675, 0.065, 0.0625, 0.0600]
  • boosting_type: ["gbdt"]
  • objective: ["binary"]

Results:

  • best_score_selected_features (the mean CV ROC AUC on D1)
  • best_params_selected_features (the hyperparameters chosen for FS1)
In [7]:
%%capture
estimator_params = {
    "n_estimators": [100, 250, 500, 1000, 2000],
    "learning_rate": [0.070, 0.0675, 0.065, 0.0625, 0.0600],
    "boosting_type": ["gbdt"], 
    "objective": ["binary"],
}

best_score_selected_features, best_params_selected_features = hyperparameter_search_helper(
    X=X_preprocess,
    y=y_preprocess,
    feature_names=sf.selected_features,
    n_splits=n_splits,
    n_repeats=n_repeats,
    hyperparameter_search=GridSearchCV,
    estimator_class=estimator_class,
    estimator_params=estimator_params,
    scoring=scoring,
)

1.2 Unbiased Evaluation on D2 (ROC Curves)¶

With features (FS1) and hyperparameters fixed from D1, we estimate performance on D2 via repeated k-fold CV and plot ROC curves. This yields an unbiased ROC AUC distribution and its mean.

In [9]:
# Train and test the model
refit_helper_selected_features = RefitHelper(
    n_splits=n_splits,
    n_repeats=n_repeats,
    feature_names=sf.selected_features,
    estimator_class=estimator_class,
    estimator_params=best_params_selected_features,
    scoring=scoring,
)
sf.selected_features
refit_helper_selected_features.feature_names = sf.selected_features
refit_helper_selected_features.fit(X_final, pd.Series(y_final))

# Plot performance estimates
fig, ax = plot_roc_curve(df=refit_helper_selected_features.history)

# Save figure
plt.tight_layout()
fig.savefig('img/fs1_roc_auc.png', dpi=300)

1.3 Cross-Validation Results (by Fold)¶

Display per-fold metrics at multiple probability thresholds.

In [10]:
pd.set_option("display.max_rows", None)

# Helper function to extract and subsequently aggregate results
def extract_stats(df):
    dfs_list = [] 
    for fold, row in df.iterrows():
        _df = pd.DataFrame(data = row["score"]["conf_matrices"])
        _df["fold"] = fold
        dfs_list.append(_df)
    stats_df = pd.concat(dfs_list).set_index(["fold"])
    return stats_df, stats_df.groupby(["probability"]).mean()

# Extract results
stats_df, stats_mean = extract_stats(df=refit_helper_selected_features.history)

Model M2: A Single Feature (FS2)¶

In this model, we restrict the input to a single type of measurement, i.e., the Maximal anterior–posterior diameter (cm), i.e., the goal is to evaluate how well this individual feature alone can discriminate between classes, and to provide an interpretable baseline against which more complex feature sets (FS1 and FS3) can be compared.

2.1 Hyperparameter Tuning on D1¶

We tune LGBMClassifier hyperparameters on D1 using repeated k-fold CV with ROC AUC as the performance measure. The grid of values below define the used search ranges:

  • n_estimators: [100, 250, 500, 1000, 2000]
  • learning_rate: [0.070, 0.0675, 0.065, 0.0625, 0.0600]
  • boosting_type: ["gbdt"]
  • objective: ["binary"]

Results:

  • best_score_single_feature (the mean CV ROC AUC on D1)
  • best_params_single_feature (the hyperparameters chosen for FS2)
In [14]:
%%capture
best_score_single_feature, best_params_single_feature = hyperparameter_search_helper(
    X=X_preprocess,
    y=y_preprocess,
    feature_names=[feature_name_mapping["ap_dia_max_ct"]],
    n_splits=n_splits,
    n_repeats=n_repeats,
    hyperparameter_search=GridSearchCV,
    estimator_class=estimator_class,
    estimator_params=estimator_params,
    scoring=scoring,
)

With features (FS2) and hyperparameters fixed from D1, we estimate performance on D2 via repeated k-fold CV and plot ROC curves. This yields an unbiased ROC AUC distribution and its mean.

4. Combined Analyses¶

4.1 Mean ROC Curves: M1 vs M2 vs M3¶

In the following, we compare the mean ROC curves for all three models by averaging the True Positive Rate (TPR) across CV folds at a common set of False Positive (FPR) values. For each model, the legend reports the AUC of the mean ROC curve along with the standard deviation of fold-level AUCs (+/- standard deviation), summarizing variability across folds. This plot highlights relative sensitivity-specificity trade-offs between:

  • M1 (FS1): Using ShapFire-selected features
  • M2 (FS3): Using a Single feature: maximal anterior–posterior diameter
  • M3 (FS2): Using all features
In [25]:
def extract_statistics(df):
    # Make sure valid data pertaining to the 'roc_auc' scoring function is
    # actually available and set in the 'self.shapfire._history' dataframe
    try:
        dict_: dict[str, typing.Any] = df["score"].iat[0]
        fpr, tpr, roc_auc = dict_["fpr"], dict_["tpr"], dict_["roc_auc"]
    except KeyError:
        raise ValueError(
            "This plotting function can only be called if valid data "
            + "pertaining to the 'roc_auc' score is availble.."
        )
    # Extract necessary data for plotting
    tprs = []
    aucs = []
    mean_fpr = np.linspace(start=0, stop=1, num=100)
    counter = 1
    for _, row in df.iterrows():
        score: dict[str, typing.Any] = row["score"]
        fpr, tpr, roc_auc = score["fpr"], score["tpr"], score["roc_auc"]
        # Plot individual ROC lines
        counter += 1

        # Perform one-dimensional linear interpolation for monotonically
        # increasing sample points
        interp_tpr = np.interp(x=mean_fpr, xp=fpr, fp=tpr)
        interp_tpr[0] = 0.0
        tprs.append(interp_tpr)
        aucs.append(roc_auc)

    # Plot mean of ROC lines
    mean_tpr = np.mean(tprs, axis=0)
    mean_tpr[-1] = 1.0
    mean_auc = auc(mean_fpr, mean_tpr)
    std_auc = np.std(aucs, ddof=1)
    return mean_fpr, mean_tpr, mean_auc, std_auc

fig, ax = plt.subplots(nrows=1, ncols=1, figsize=(10, 3.5))

mean_fpr, mean_tpr, mean_auc, std_auc = extract_statistics(refit_helper_selected_features.history)
ax.plot(
    mean_fpr, mean_tpr,
    linewidth=2.5,
    label=f"ShapFire-Selected Features:\n" + r"Mean ROC (AUC = %0.2f $\pm$ %0.2f)" % (mean_auc, std_auc),
)

mean_fpr, mean_tpr, mean_auc, std_auc = extract_statistics(refit_helper_baseline_features.history)
ax.plot(
    mean_fpr, mean_tpr,
    linewidth=2.5,
    label=f"All Features:\n" + r"Mean ROC (AUC = %0.2f $\pm$ %0.2f)" % (mean_auc, std_auc)
)

mean_fpr, mean_tpr, mean_auc, std_auc = extract_statistics(refit_helper_single_feature.history)
ax.plot(
    mean_fpr, mean_tpr,
    linewidth=2.5,
    label=f"Maximal Diameter of the AAA Only:\n" + r"Mean ROC (AUC = %0.2f $\pm$ %0.2f)" % (mean_auc, std_auc),
)
ax.grid(True)
plt.title("Mean ROC Curves",fontsize=12)
plt.xlabel("False Positive Rate", fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel("True Positive Rate", fontsize=12)
plt.legend(fontsize=12, fancybox=True)
plt.yticks(fontsize=12)
plt.xticks(fontsize=12)
fig.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
fig.savefig('img/m1_m2_m3_comparison.png', dpi=300)

4.2 Hypothesis Testing¶

To assess whether differences in model performance are statistically significant, we use paired tests on the per-fold ROC AUC values obtained from identical CV splits. Specifically, we apply paired t-tests to compare mean ROC AUCs between models.

The code below collects the per-fold ROC AUC values for each model type (M1, M2, M3), which serve as the paired inputs for hypothesis testing.

In [26]:
single_feature_roc_auc = [] 
selected_feature_roc_auc = [] 
baseline_feature_roc_auc = [] 
for i in range(0, 4):
    single_feature_roc_auc.append(refit_helper_single_feature.history["score"].iat[i]["roc_auc"])
    selected_feature_roc_auc.append(refit_helper_selected_features.history["score"].iat[i]["roc_auc"])
    baseline_feature_roc_auc.append(refit_helper_baseline_features.history["score"].iat[i]["roc_auc"])

4.3 Save Models¶

To prepare models for external validation and downstream use, we re-train each final classifier on the entire dataset using the different feature sets and tuned hyperparameters. In this context, the helper function save_artifacts exports the following artifacts:

  • Model: LightGBM booster saved in native format (model.txt).
  • Feature schema (schema.json):
    • strict feature order,
    • pandas dtypes,
    • categorical feature list,
    • missing-value policy,
    • label policy (threshold used).
  • Parameters & metadata (params.json):
    • hyperparameters,
    • best iteration (if available),
    • class labels,
    • optional notes.
In [33]:
def save_artifacts(
    clf: lgb.LGBMClassifier,
    X,
    export_dir="export",
    threshold: float = 0.5,
    notes: str = ""
):
    p = Path(export_dir); p.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    # Save model
    booster = clf.booster_
    model_path = p / "model.txt"
    booster.save_model(str(model_path))

    # Save feature schema
    feature_names = list(X.columns)
    dtypes = {c: str(X[c].dtype) for c in feature_names}
    # If native categorical features are used, store them explicitly
    cat_feats = getattr(clf, "categorical_feature_", None)
    if cat_feats is None:
        # Otherwise fall back to anything that looks categorical
        cat_feats = [c for c in feature_names if isinstance(X[c], pd.CategoricalDtype) or X[c].dtype == "object"]

    schema = {
        "feature_names": feature_names,             # strict order!
        "dtypes": dtypes,                           # pandas dtype strings
        "categorical_feature": list(cat_feats),     # columns treated as categorical
        "missing_value_policy": "pass-through (NaN)",
        "label_policy": {"type": "threshold", "threshold": threshold},  # for classifiers
    }
    (p / "schema.json").write_text(json.dumps(schema, indent=2))

    # Save params & training metadata
    params = clf.get_params(deep=True)
    meta = {
        "params": params,
        "best_iteration": getattr(clf, "best_iteration_", None),
        "classes_": getattr(clf, "classes_", None) if hasattr(clf, "classes_") else None,
        "notes": notes,
    }
    (p / "params.json").write_text(
        json.dumps(meta, indent=2, default=lambda o: o if isinstance(o, (int, float, str, list, dict, type(None))) else str(o))
    )

    # # Save environment info
    # env_lines = [
    #     f"python: {platform.python_version()}",
    #     f"lightgbm: {lgb.__version__}",
    #     f"numpy: {np.__version__}",
    #     f"pandas: {pd.__version__}",
    #     "hardware: GPU" if "gpu" in str(params).lower() else "hardware: CPU",
    # ]
    # (p / "env.txt").write_text("\n".join(env_lines))

X = pd.concat([X_preprocess, X_final])
y = pd.concat([y_preprocess, y_final])
